key_points: A 44-year-old Lithuanian rower, Aurimas Mockus, was rescued by the Australian Navy after his boat was damaged by Tropical Cyclone Alfred while he was attempting a solo, nonstop row across the Pacific from California to Brisbane.
He was stranded for three days in the Coral Sea before rescuers made radio contact and brought him aboard a warship heading to Sydney.

The passage recounts earlier Pacific rowing attempts, including Peter Bird's partially assisted 1983 crossing, John Beeden's 2015 crossing, Michelle Lee becoming the first woman to complete it in 2023, and Tom Robinson's rescue near Vanuatu after 265 days at sea in 2023.
Mockus was attempting to join the small group of people who have crossed the Pacific alone and without stopping.
main_idea: A Lithuanian rower's attempt to cross the Pacific alone ended in a dramatic Australian Navy rescue after a tropical cyclone destroyed his boat, joining a short history of difficult and sometimes incomplete solo Pacific crossings.
restate_sentence: The 44-year-old adventurer began his trip alone in October from San Diego, California.
